# At positive rates, the truncated entropy stress is an integrated moving-hinge payment

This calculation uses the ACTUAL selected-minimum scalar stress and the
SAME separator and scale. It identifies exactly what the new truncated
relative-entropy physical tests add at the rate-measure level. By
themselves they give an integral of the already proved moving-hinge tail
inequalities. The stronger discounted coupling theorem still needs an
actual distinct-endpoint branch before it can produce another numerical
cap payment.

## 1. Actual selected-minimum data

Use the hypotheses and notation of
candidate 06f3c3316a88c7ba:

    Xi_j=W_j-beta_j+r_j+R_j,
    r_j=lambda_j(-log L_j)_+,
    lambda_j->0, beta_j->beta, |R_j|<=C lambda_j.

The actual full log-weighted surface and cap-load measures have jointly
retained limits bhat and ahat over the zero set, with rates in [0,beta].
The ordinary parts have rate zero. Retain the same actual cap selectors
and probability law; no source or cap labels are reassigned.

Let q be a nonnegative finite globally convex physical function, bounded
on the common compact support, and psi a nonnegative continuous normal
weight. Fix R>0. The truncated entropy from the audited root note is

    F(q,D)=sup_(t>=0)[tq-(exp(t)-1)D].

The current field

    Phi_j(n,w)=psi(n) F(q(w),exp(R/lambda_j)L_j(w))       (1)

is globally finite convex in physical w. Indeed use the finite-plane
extension and bound the maximizing t on the current compact body; its
bound may depend on j. Thus (1) is an ACTUAL permitted physical speed
for the same separator, not an extrapolated formal derivative.

## 2. Uniform asymptotics on the positive-rate region

Write Q=max q on the common compact set. If Q=0 the field is zero.
Otherwise its support satisfies

    r_j>=R-lambda_j log Q,

so eventually it is contained in r_j>=R/2. On this support L_j<1
for large j, and L_j=exp(-r_j/lambda_j) exactly.

Uniformly for 0<=q<=Q and r in a common compact rate interval,

    lambda_j F(q,exp((R-r)/lambda_j))
          -> q(r-R)_+.                                (2)

The error is O(lambda_j). To see this for r>=R, use the explicit branch
F=q log q+q(r-R)/lambda_j-q+D when q>D, where D=exp((R-r)/lambda_j)<=1.
The terms q log q, q, and D are uniformly bounded. If q<=D, the entropy
vanishes, while q(r-R)<=D(r-R)<=lambda_j/e. If r<R, positivity requires
D<q<=Q, so r is within O(lambda_j) of R and F is uniformly bounded.
This proves (2), including q=0 and rate atoms at R.

The exact identity d eta_j/lambda_j=d(logmeasure_j)/r_j on the support
therefore converts the main stress terms to integrals against the
retained log measures, with bounded weight

    lambda_j Phi_j/r_j -> psi q (r-R)_+/r.

The uniformly O(lambda_j) remainder contributes o(1): its absolute
integral is at most C lambda_j times a uniformly bounded integral of
(lambda_j Phi_j)/r_j against the log measure. Ordinary rate-zero terms
vanish because of the support restriction. Joint weak convergence and
the uniform approximation (2) now give

    integral psi q (r-R)_+/r dahat
       +integral psi q (r-R)_+ dbhat
       <=beta integral psi q (r-R)_+/r dbhat.            (3)

The factor at r=R is zero. There is no open/closed threshold ambiguity.
All coefficients are those of the actual same-separator normalization.

## 3. Exact implication from the earlier moving-hinge tails

For each T>0 the existing theorem already gives

    integral_(r>T) psi q/r dahat
       +integral_(r>T) psi q dbhat
       <=beta integral_(r>T) psi q/r dbhat.             (4)

Integrate (4) in T from R to beta. Tonelli on each positive term and
integral_R^beta 1_(r>T)dT=(r-R)_+ prove EXACTLY (3).
Thus the rate inequality obtained from (1) adds no constraint beyond
(4). It is not necessary to subtract two inequalities or to differentiate
a separator inequality.

Homogeneity also handles an exponentially scaled numerator: for fixed S,

    F(exp(S/lambda)q,exp(R/lambda)L)
       =exp(S/lambda)F(q,exp((R-S)/lambda)L).

After dividing the stress by the positive prefactor, this is simply the
same threshold translated from R to R-S, whenever that threshold remains
positive. Hence this scalar rescaling is not a new positive-rate test.

## 4. Canonical inverse-density form

Fix a legitimate gradient direction e and retain its full cap law.
After the existing signed section bookkeeping, put

    V(T)=integral q dv_e(T),
    C(T)=integral q dv_e^noninside(T).

The earlier pointwise payment is

    C(T)+T V(T)+integral_T^beta V(s)ds<=beta V(T).        (5)

Integrating (5) over T in [R,beta] gives

    integral_R^beta C(T)dT
       +2 integral_R^beta T V(T)dT
       <=(beta+R) integral_R^beta V(T)dT.               (6)

This is the canonical inverse-density consequence of the truncated
entropy test after dropping inside section exceptions. It is just the
integrated moving-hinge payment; no new captured-mass lower bound appears.
The coefficient two comes from interchanging the triangular tail integral
and is exact. Positive rate atoms are retained through the canonical
right/left versions of (5); a single endpoint has zero dT measure.

## 5. Precise consequence for the proof search

The truncated entropy IS a new useful quantitative coupling bound,
particularly for convex hinge weights and their explicit crossing costs.
But its direct selected-minimum scalar stress limit has now been proved
to reduce to an existing positive-rate inequality. A new numerical gain
must therefore use the actual repaired coupling, its distinct endpoint
capacities, or a further geometric incidence relation. Merely inserting
the entropy field into the same physical stress and invoking the uniform
kernel does not strengthen (5).
